plain_policy: Find a table for the built-in L banquette that Angela likes (about 48 x 32 in, pill or boat shaped, on a pedestal) and say exactly how it sits. Nothing may collide; the walk from the kitchen to the dining room must stay at least 24 inches with the chairs pushed in; a banquette seat only counts if there are at least 9 inches between the back cushion and the table edge. Everything else is a trade-off measured against today's table. Priorities in order: the kitchen-to-dining walkway, room to slide into and sit on both benches, two comfortable everyday seats and four with guests, Angela's size and style, cost.

ranking: filter invalid; cluster by (table shape and size class, long axis, overlap pattern, number of chairs); pick distinct representatives; rank EVERY shown layout (Today, generated, pinned, council) on one scale, lexicographically by bands: (1) walk to the dining room with a chair on the open side seated: 30+ comfortable, 24-30 tight, below 24 minimal; (2) reach from each bench used daily: table edge over the seat front by 0-4 in, or cushion-to-edge 9-13 in = comfortable; 13-15 = a lean; over 15 or a gap beyond the seat front = too far; under 9 = cramped; (3) Angela's preference: length 44-53 and width 28-34 with pill, boat, racetrack or oval shape and a pedestal or plate base = strong; one of those off = partial; round or rectangle under 40 long = weak; (4) style fit (walnut or warm oak, mid-century form); (5) seats at the table; (6) available without a custom quote; (7) lower cost. Show Today plus the top four distinct layouts first (any source; label council picks as such), then fold the rest under 'More options (n)'. Each card states its rank and one trade-off sentence.

plain_text.layout_sentence: one sentence of at most 25 words per layout, saying what changes and its main trade-off (e.g. '48 x 32 pill, 2 in over both benches: 11 in of body room, 3 in less than you would like, kitchen walkway unchanged.')
plain_text.verdict: at most three short sentences at the top: does Angela's 48 x 32 fit and how it sits; the best in-stock match; the one measurement that matters most
plain_text.details: full measures per layout with +/- and the difference from Today in an expandable section and the tables

rotation: table long axis east-west or north-south; round tables centred on the corner diagonal; chairs on any open side. Prune, but report how many arrangements were evaluated.
